title: Research facet-rs export serialization backend
description: Investigate whether facet-rs can be used as an export serialization backend alongside or instead of serde_json for niri export records, and whether it reduces adapter boilerplate or supports feature-gated serializer backends.
design: Research facet-rs capabilities with external types from niri_ipc, derived vs non-derived reflection, JSON output support, feature gating, and trait-based serializer abstraction. Compare against serde_json::Value, custom Serialize impls, and macro-generated adapters. Produce a recommendation before implementation.
acceptance_criteria:
- Research notes compare facet-rs with current serde implementation.
- Determine whether niri_ipc external types can be serialized without changing upstream.
- Identify required dependencies/features and binary impact concerns.
- Recommend whether to implement, defer, or reject facet backend.
- If recommended, outline the trait boundary for multiple export serializers.

title: Add nested field filters for export records
description: Extend export filtering beyond top-level record kind/id/type selectors to support nested field predicates such as `window.app_id=kitty`, `output.logical.width=2560`, and `cast.target.window=123`. Filters should continue to be predicates that may match zero or more records.
design: Keep existing filters (`window`, `window=4`, `type=...`) as shorthand. Add a parser representation that can handle dotted field paths, typed values, and nested enum-like payloads. Avoid hardcoding only current examples; design the matcher so additional niri_ipc fields can be added incrementally. Consider whether matching should use typed accessors, serde_json::Value projection, or a hybrid approach.
acceptance_criteria:
- Existing filters remain backward compatible.
- Nested filters can match at least window app_id, output logical dimensions, and cast target window/output.
- Invalid field paths produce useful errors.
- Tests cover zero, one, and many matches for nested predicates.
- Documentation explains that filters are ORed and can match multiple records.

title: Print stream export state on SIGUSR1
description: When running niri export streaming, support an application diagnostic signal that prints current state without stopping the stream.
design: Use SIGUSR1 on Unix as the initial signal because it is conventionally application-defined and does not imply reload or shutdown. When received during `export --stream`, emit a snapshot/state dump using the active export filters and projection options where feasible. Document that SIGUSR1 support is Unix-specific unless a later cross-platform mechanism is added.
acceptance_criteria:
- `export --stream` handles SIGUSR1 without terminating.
- Receiving SIGUSR1 emits current export state or a clearly defined snapshot record set.
- Output uses the same writer path as normal export records.
- Behavior is documented, including that SIGUSR1 is assigned by zooming-kittens and is not a niri event.
- Non-Unix behavior is explicitly handled or documented as unsupported.

title: Add unpacked stream export records
description: Add --unpack support for niri stream export so batch events can be emitted as multiple per-entity or per-change records while preserving a shared synthetic stream_event_id for regrouping.
design: Default stream output should remain faithful: one niri event becomes one output record. --unpack may split events such as WindowLayoutsChanged into one record per changed window. Include stream_event_id on unpacked records so consumers can associate records that came from the same original niri event.
acceptance_criteria:
- --unpack emits per-change/per-entity records for supported batch events.
- Unpacked records include stream_event_id.
- Default stream mode remains one output record per niri event.
- Tests cover WindowLayoutsChanged and at least one non-batch event.

title: Persist stream event id resume state
description: Add support for automatically persisting and resuming the starting stream event id for niri event exports. The stream command will initially support an explicit --starting-id with a default of 1; this follow-up should define where resume state lives, how it is keyed, and how users opt in/out of persisted counters.
design: Consider XDG state storage keyed by compositor/session/socket identity if available. The persisted id is synthetic zooming-kittens state, not a niri-provided event id. Avoid implying stability across unrelated niri sessions unless we can prove the key is safe.
acceptance_criteria:
- Users can enable persisted stream event ids without manually passing --starting-id.
- Documentation states ids are assigned by zooming-kittens and are not niri ids.
- State storage location and reset behavior are explicit.
- Tests cover starting from persisted state and resetting/overriding it.

title: Support additional terminals beyond kitty
description:
The zoomer and font control features are currently kitty-specific, using kitty's remote control socket protocol (via the kitty-rc crate). The core architecture (niri event stream -> resizer) is terminal-agnostic. We should add support for additional terminals.

Likely candidates:
- **Alacritty**: config-file based (requires file watch + reload, or SIGUSR1)
- **Foot**: IPC socket support, `foot --server` mode
- **WezTerm**: multiplexer API via CLI
- **Ghostty**: check available IPC

The implementation should abstract terminal interaction behind a trait so that zoomer/longcat don't need to know which terminal they're talking to. The existing KittyResizer becomes one implementation.

Acceptance criteria:
- Terminal backend trait that abstracts font-size operations
- Kitty implementation as the first backend (refactored from current code)
- At least one additional terminal backend (foot recommended as it has good IPC)
- CLI flag or config option to select terminal backend
- README updated to list supported terminals

title: Handle user layout modifications in longcat (window moves, etc.)
description:
Investigate and handle user-driven layout modifications in longcat, such as moving a window into a column. Currently longcat responds to focus events but doesn't detect when the user manually rearranges windows (e.g., moving a window to a different column, adding/removing windows from a column).

Need to:
1. Detect when windows enter/exit a column
2. Understand niri's layout change events that indicate window movement
3. Update column state appropriately when layouts are modified by user actions
4. Possibly restore original heights or recalculate proportions when column composition changes

title: Add dry run mode for longcat
description:
Add a dry run mode for longcat that prints what window height changes would be applied without actually applying them. This is useful for debugging and testing the longcat behavior without affecting actual window layouts.

Should add a CLI flag like --dry-run or -d to the longcat subcommand, and make Longcat track but skip the send_action() calls when in dry run mode.

title: Create shared niri connection pool for commands
description:
Currently NiriRegistry creates new connections on every focus event in get_window_info(). Each focus change triggers 2 new connections (one for focused window, one for blurred window). We need to implement a shared connection pool similar to how Longcat handles niri_socket, so that queries and actions reuse connections rather than creating new ones each time.

Key issue: src/niri/registry.rs:176 - Socket::connect() called on every get_window_info() invocation

title: Investigate: multiple columns changing height simultaneously
description: Bug report: sometimes multiple columns both change height when only one should be affected. Need to identify the root cause and fix the behavior so that height changes are isolated to the intended column only.

title: longcat: clear original status & reset window sizes on column blur
description: Ensure longcat clears its original status and resets window sizes whenever focus leaves the current column.

title: Auto-detect kitty PID via environment variables
description: Automatically detect Kitty terminal emulator PID using environment variables instead of requiring manual configuration
acceptance_criteria:
Identify relevant Kitty environment variables (e.g., KITTY_PID, KITTY_WINDOW_ID)
Implement PID detection logic that checks environment variables
Fallback gracefully if env vars not present
Update documentation to mention auto-detection capability

title: Enhance zooming status JSON output with structured data
description:
Add detailed zooming status to focus event JSON output.

Currently, when kitty focus changes, we only emit basic events. We need to add structured data about font adjustment operations.

## Requirements

### Focus Gained Event
Add `zooming` field with structured status:
- `status`: "success" | "not_configured" | "connection_failed" | "auth_failed"
- `pid`: kitty process ID
- `font_adjustment`: "+3" (always)
- When successful: include adjustment details
- When failed: include error reason

Example:
```json
{
  "event": "focus_gained",
  "window_id": 12345,
  "app_id": "kitty",
  "zooming": {
    "status": "success",
    "pid": 45678,
    "font_adjustment": "+3"
  }
}
```

### Focus Lost Event
Add `zooming` field for single kitty:
- `status`: "success" | "failed"
- `pid`: kitty process ID (the one that lost focus)
- `font_adjustment`: "-3" (always)
- When failed: include error

Example:
```json
{
  "event": "focus_lost",
  "zooming": {
    "status": "success",
    "pid": 45678,
    "font_adjustment": "-3"
  }
}
```

## Notes
- Focus lost should only affect ONE kitty at a time (the one that just lost focus)
- Not all kitty instances have remote control configured
- No message field needed - use structured data only
- Status values should be machine-readable

title: Add structured JSON output mode
description:
The old README described JSON lines output to stdout, but the current code only uses eprintln for human-readable logging. We should add a proper structured JSON output mode that writes event data (focus gained/lost, font size changes, longcat height adjustments) as JSON lines to stdout. This would make the tool composable with other Unix tools and enable scripting use cases.

Acceptance criteria:
- `--output json` (or similar) flag that switches from human-readable stderr logging to structured JSON lines on stdout
- Each event type (focus, blur, font change, height change) has a defined JSON schema
- Human-readable logging stays on stderr regardless of output mode
- Existing behavior (eprintln to stderr) remains the default

title: Fix focus-lost to only affect the kitty that lost focus
description:
When focus is lost, the current implementation iterates through ALL kitty windows to decrease font size. This is incorrect - we should only affect the kitty that just lost focus.

Current buggy behavior:
- Focus lost event triggers
- Code iterates through ALL kitty windows
- Decreases font size in ALL kitty instances

Required fix:
- Track which kitty currently has focus when focus is gained
- On focus lost, only affect the kitty that just lost focus
- Clear the focus tracker after handling
